paper_metadata.title: Addition of nitrogen in Ni-based cast Superalloys: Microstructures and properties

evidence.quote: This study comprehensively investigated the nitrogen-induced effects on microstructural characteristics and creep performance in Ni-based cast superalloys, with focus on microsegregation and inclusion evolution.

Nickel-based casting superalloys have dual-phase structures of γ matrix and γ ′ precipitation, which are stable at high temperatures and display excellent mechanical properties and ductility at extreme temperatures through the precipitation strengthening mechanism
Fig. 2 (e – h) demonstrates the γ matrix and γ ′ phase of superalloys with different N amounts. The γ ′ phase was cubic and neatly distributed in the matrix.
As the N content increased, the number and density of MC carbides and γ / γ ′ eutectics decreased, and the morphology of MC carbides changed from rod-like to blocky form.
Fig. 2 (a – d) demonstrates that MC carbides and γ / γ ′ eutectics coexisted in interdendritic regions, with their morphology showing changes at different N levels.

First-principles calculations demonstrated that TiN inclusions preferentially form during solidification and serve as heterogeneous nucleation cores, thereby refining the grain structure.
Experimental results demonstrated that increasing nitrogen content from 4 ppm to 55 ppm led to progressive intensification of elemental segregation.
As illustrated in Fig. 9 (a), rod-like MC carbides were prone to stress concentration and cracked to form microcracks in low-nitrogen alloys.
